author: Claude
candidate_edge: A single volatility-expansion signal per weekday on XAUUSD, gated strictly to the 13:30-14:30 UTC US cash/COMEX-linked open window, flat by 20:00 UTC (0% overnight). Bounded params: reference range = 12:30-13:30 UTC pre-open range, entry = M15-confirmed close beyond that range in the 13:30-14:30 UTC window, stop = reference-range width, target = 1.5x-2.0x reference-range width, hard time-stop flat at 20:00 UTC.
confidence: Low-to-moderate. Gold's elevated volatility around 13:30 UTC (many high-impact USD macro releases print at 08:30 ET) is a widely observed market microstructure fact, but the two existing always-on gold H1 EAs that already show high density+edge in the frozen screen (10423, 11690) both FAILED Q05 on drawdown -- so the open question is specifically whether session-gating (0% overnight, one signal/day) fixes the drawdown failure mode without destroying the edge, not whether gold has a tradeable edge at all. This is a narrower and more falsifiable claim than 'gold is volatile at the US open'.
confounders: The 13:30 UTC window overlaps the mandatory news blackout for high-impact USD releases; if the tradeable move is driven by the same releases the blackout excludes, density could collapse well below the structural prior once the filter is applied.

Gold's point value and typical spread are materially different from FX majors; the qualitative cost-to-target check below is not a substitute for a real commission read from framework/registry/tester_defaults.json.

10700 XAUUSD (in the current demo roster) already carries 58% overnight exposure and a 19.7h hold at a healthy +0.165R/trade -- if H-V2's session-flat redesign simply captures a subset of the SAME underlying gold edge as 10700 rather than a genuinely distinct one, the two would be correlated day-to-day and should not both enter a book without the joint-tail check.

10423/11690's Q05 DD failures could stem from position sizing rather than from being always-on; if so, session-gating alone may not fix the DD axis and the falsification criterion below (DD reproduces the same failure) is designed to catch that.
observations: The two highest-density measured gold configurations in the frozen Q02 screen (10423: 0.82 trades/bd, +0.086R/trade; 11690: 1.84 trades/bd, +0.028R/trade) both show real edge but both FAILED Q05 on drawdown (41% and 59% respectively, per README.md's velocity table) -- they are always-on H1 signals, not gated to a specific session. The current demo-roster gold sleeve (10700) achieves +0.165R/trade but only at 0.18 trades/bd with 58% overnight exposure and a 19.7h hold. No measured configuration combines XAUUSD's demonstrated H1 edge with a session-flat (0% overnight), single-window structure the way 13213 does for USDJPY.
proposed_mechanism: Gold is a global 23/5 OTC market whose volatility genuinely clusters around the US cash-equity/COMEX-linked open (13:30 UTC / 08:30 ET), a window in which a large share of high-impact USD macro data prints -- unlike the H-CW/H-MR index trio (41475/41476), whose 'cash-open' anchor is CORRECT for US-listed symbols but demonstrably mistimed for GDAXI (5-6h late per FTMO_PORTFOLIO_GAP_CURRENT.md section 7). XAUUSD has no such timing mismatch because it trades continuously and its own volatility genuinely concentrates at this window regardless of which exchange is 'open'. H-V2 asks whether capturing that expansion in a single session-gated (0% overnight) trade per day reproduces gold's already-measured H1 edge (10423/11690) while fixing the drawdown failure that killed both existing always-on configurations.

quantitative_claims.claim: 10423 and 11690 (always-on XAUUSD H1) show real density+edge but both failed Q05 on drawdown
10700 (demo roster XAUUSD sleeve) profile used as the always-on comparison point
measured XAUUSD Q02 configuration ceiling/floor across all 70 configurations in the frozen screen
